# The Art Story

> > A comprehensive educational resource for modern and contemporary art history, featuring artists like Picasso, Rothko, Matisse, and Warhol, major art movements, and critical ideas that shaped visual art from 1850 to the present.

The Art Story provides in-depth profiles of artists, movements, and concepts in modern art history, with unique educational tools including image comparison features, interactive timelines, and specialized initiatives like the Jewish Modern Art project. Founded by Michael Zurakhinsky, the site serves students, researchers, and art enthusiasts with scholarly content on museums, galleries, and the evolution of avant-garde art.

## Key Topics

- Modern Art (1850-1970)
- Contemporary Art
- Abstract Expressionism
- Pop Art
- Art Movements and Avant-Garde
- Mark Rothko
- Henri Matisse
- Marcel Duchamp
- Edvard Munch
- Image Comparison Methodology
- Jewish Artists in Modern Art
- Museum History (MoMA, Guggenheim)
- New York School
- Paris Art Scene
- Art Education and Research

## Core Resources

- [The Art Story: Visual Art Movements, Artists, Ideas and Topics](https://www.theartstory.org): Homepage featuring Picasso, Warhol, Basquiat and art movements overview
- [The Ideas of Art: Including Historians and Influencers](https://www.theartstory.org/ideas): Art concepts, techniques and theory from Chiaroscuro to Renaissance
- [Jewish Modern Art Initiative](https://www.theartstory.org/jewish-art.htm): Jewish Modern Art Initiative featuring Rothko, Chagall and timeline
- [About The Founder](https://www.theartstory.org/about-us-founder.htm): Founder Michael Zurakhinsky's story and Art Story mission

## Timelines and Reference

- [Modern Art Top 50 Timeline](https://www.theartstory.org/top50.htm): Interactive timeline of 50 most important modern artworks 1850-1970
- [Modern Art Jewish Timeline](https://www.theartstory.org/timeline-jewish.htm): Chronology of Jewish artists' achievements in modern art
- [Museum of Modern Art Overview](https://www.theartstory.org/venue/museum-of-modern-art): MoMA history from founding by Rockefeller to present leadership
- [The Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum](https://www.theartstory.org/museum-guggenheim.htm): Profile of Guggenheim Museum history from 1939 founding to present
- [Florence Map - City Art Highlights](https://www.theartstory.org/maps/florence.htm): Interactive map of Florence's most important artworks and museums

## Image Comparison Tools

- [Image Comparison Tool - Main](https://www.theartstory.org/comparison-main.htm): Educational tool comparing modern artists to classical masters
- [Image Comparison - Edvard Munch - Main](https://www.theartstory.org/comparison-munch-edvard.htm): Munch's Scream and Sick Child compared to Krohg and Van Gogh
- [Rothko vs. Friedrich: The Void](https://www.theartstory.org/comparison-rothko-mark-1.htm): Comparing Rothko's abstraction to Friedrich's Romantic landscapes
- [Image Comparison - Courbet vs. Bouguereau: The Body](https://www.theartstory.org/comparison-courbet-3.htm): Visual comparison: Courbet's Realism vs Bouguereau's classical style
- [Image Comparison - Matisse vs. Carracci: Decoration](https://www.theartstory.org/comparison-matisse-2.htm): Matisse's Dance II compared to Carracci's classical decoration

## Gallery and Venue Profiles

- [The Charles Egan Gallery](https://www.theartstory.org/gallery-egan-charles.htm): Charles Egan Gallery history featuring de Kooning and New York School
- [The Julien Levy Gallery](https://www.theartstory.org/gallery-levy-julien.htm): Julien Levy Gallery profile: Surrealism, photography and Ernst

## For Students and Researchers

- [For Researchers](https://www.theartstory.org/researchers.htm): Research tools and citation resources for academic art history study
- [Student Ambassador Program](https://www.theartstory.org/ambassadors.htm): Student program for art writing and social media marketing experience

## Optional

- [New Artists, Movements, Ideas added to The Art Story](https://www.theartstory.org/new-pages-on-the-art-story): Latest additions to site content including artists and movements
